note: Defines long chain of thought against short, and names overthinking and inference time scaling as measurable phenomena.
title: Towards Reasoning Era: A Survey of Long Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Large Language Models
explain_beginner: Recent AI models like OpenAI-o1 have become better at solving hard problems by thinking through multiple steps before answering. This paper explains the difference between simple, quick thinking and extended, detailed reasoning. The extended approach lets models explore more possibilities and catch mistakes along the way, producing better answers. The survey clarifies how and why this longer thinking process works, addresses debates about whether models overthink problems, and identifies areas where this approach needs improvement.
explain_business: Organizations should understand that AI systems now benefit from spending more computation time on difficult problems through extended reasoning processes. This extended approach produces more reliable answers for complex tasks in mathematics and programming, but requires accepting longer inference times. Decision-makers must weigh the tradeoff between speed and accuracy for their applications. This survey identifies efficiency gains and knowledge integration as near-term opportunities to make extended reasoning more practical and cost-effective for enterprise deployment.
explain_practitioner: This survey distinguishes long chain-of-thought from short variants and proposes a taxonomy of reasoning paradigms. Long CoT exhibits three key properties: deep reasoning, extensive exploration, and feasible reflection. The authors analyze emergence phenomena including overthinking and inference-time scaling effects. They document how these characteristics enable models to solve complex mathematical and coding tasks more effectively than shallow approaches. The paper identifies research gaps in multimodal integration, computational efficiency, and knowledge frameworks, establishing a foundation for future reasoning model development.
